thread:
liam: Quick question — who has the canonical list of checks/features that must remain identical across hosted/dedicated/private? I'm mapping auth, routing, and fallback behavior.
maria: We don't have a single doc yet, just scattered RFC notes. High-level: authz/authn, KMS usage, and billing attribution are the tricky ones.
josh: +1. Also tenant isolation guarantees (data plane encryption, egress rules) differ for private.
sophia: For routing: hosted can use global smart routing + model pool, dedicated pins to a GPU pool, private is local. That changes fallback semantics.
liam: Right — I'm trying to capture invariants vs implementation levers. e.g., invariant: request must be authenticated and authorized for model access. implementation levers: token introspection (hosted), mTLS + internal tokens (private/dedicated).
derek: Can we make a small table? Something like: invariant / hosted impl / dedicated impl / private impl. Keep it opinionated.
maria: I sketched one in the meeting notes. Quick draft:
```
Invariant: AuthN/AuthZ -> hosted: OIDC + token introspection; dedicated: OIDC + tenant key; private: mTLS + local SSO
Invariant: Billing attribution -> hosted: token mapping; dedicated: reserved capacity mapping; private: partner billing hook
Invariant: Model variant fallback -> hosted: route to cheaper model; dedicated: fallback within pool; private: no cross-tenant fallthrough
```
josh: Important callout: private deployments may want configurable fallbacks (some customers allow a managed-hosted fallback during peak). We need a policy that can be turned on/off.
sophia: +1. Also latencies: hosted has multi-region routing which can increase p95; dedicated expects tighter SLOs per commit.
liam: So we should define a policy DSL? Something like `fallback: {allowed: bool, target: enum, auth_check: enum}` so operators can opt-in.
derek: Love the DSL idea. Keep defaults strict (no cross-env fallback unless customer explicit opt-in). Also log and audit every fallback.
infra-bot: note: existing "fallback-audit" sink exists, but retention/config is different in private installs (default 7d vs hosted 90d).
maria: Another gap: observability surface. Hosted exposes per-token cost/latency. Dedicated exposes per-reservation metrics. Private often wants only aggregated metrics — we need a shim.
josh: Implementation tradeoff: unify telemetry schema but gate PII fields based on deployment mode. That way code paths can call the same emitters.
sophia: Edge case: function-tool calling and external internet access. Hosted can call external tools. Private customers often block egress; we need a clear feature flag and a graceful error policy.
liam: Agree. Let's call that `external_io: {enabled: bool, fallback: enum}`. If disabled and a prompt needs a tool, respond with structured error explaining unavailable capability.
derek: Ops playbook: if a private cluster enables hosted-fallbacks, we must require a signed enterprise agreement and a per-request consent header. Otherwise deny.
maria: Action items: 1) Draft the invariants list (liam) 2) Proto DSL + examples (sophia) 3) Telemetry gate proposal (josh) 4) Security checklist for cross-env fallbacks (derek)
liam: I'll create the invariants doc and link here. Quick ack if anyone has changes to the action items.
sophia: ack
josh: ack
maria: ack
infra-bot: created ticket ARCH-6924 for "deployment-mode invariants and fallback DSL" (https://tickets.internal/ARCH-6924) :white_check_mark:
liam: Thanks — I'll drop the first draft into the ticket by EOD. If we can get a short RFC, we can fold into runtime-adapter surface work.
